newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police abuse of reporters rising - watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police abuse of reporters rising - watchdog.

text.p: A media freedom watchdog group said in a report released on Tuesday that a rise in abuses by Turkish police against journalists in 1996 reflected a worsening in the country's human rights record.

"The human rights situation in Turkey got worse (in 1996). This is why we decided to prepare a report on police violence on journalists at work," Jean Chichizola of Paris-based Reporters Sans Frontieres (RSF - Reporters Without Borders) told a news conference.

The RSF report said 154 journalists were victims of police abuse in 1996 -- one died, 31 were tortured in custody, 53 were beaten up and 69 were threatened. In 1995, one died, 24 were tortured, 12 beaten up and 13 threatened.
Chichizola said the RSF investigation was launched after the killing of leftist journalist Metin Goktepe in police custody in January 1996.
"We see the Goktepe incident as a turning point, we have chosen it as our symbolic case to follow and to make it more public in the world's eyes," he said.

Forty-eight policemen are being investigated over their involvement in Goktepe's death. The case has been delayed after being transferred twice to different provinces for what officials describe as security concerns.
RSF is planning to attend the next hearing of the case scheduled for February 6.
Chichizola also said there were indications of an increase in police force at public protests, adding that mainstream media is also subject to abuse.
"In Turkey, police do not only target their violence at the Kurdish and leftist media, but also against mainstream media," he said.
